claims.text: High configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered structure of near-equiatomic, multi-element solid-solution nanoparticles at high service temperatures.
High configurational entropy suppresses atomic diffusion and phase separation in these nanoparticles.
Intentionally skewed compositions have lower configurational entropy than near-equiatomic compositions.
Compositionally skewed nanoparticles exhibit more atomic segregation and phase instability than near-equiatomic nanoparticles under identical thermal conditions.
The initial near-equiatomic nanoparticles form a homogeneous, single-phase, disordered solid solution.
Changing composition from near-equiatomic to deliberately skewed while holding synthesis parameters constant provides a controlled reduction in configurational-entropy stabilization.
An inert atmosphere minimizes extrinsic oxidation effects during thermal cycling.
Atomic-scale elemental mixing maintains a disordered, single-phase structure.
High configurational entropy raises energetic barriers to atomic mobility and diffusion.
Raised barriers to atomic mobility suppress phase segregation and sintering during high-temperature exposure.
Reducing configurational entropy through a non-equiatomic composition lowers barriers to atomic mobility.
Lower barriers to atomic mobility facilitate diffusion and subsequent phase instability.
After high-temperature treatment, near-equiatomic nanoparticles will retain a more homogeneous elemental distribution with less phase separation and coarsening than skewed-composition nanoparticles.
Skewed-composition nanoparticles will show detectable elemental segregation, phase changes, and increased particle-size variation after high-temperature treatment.
Nanoparticles made under standard synthesis conditions have an intermediate degree of elemental mixing and stability at room temperature or below the onset of significant diffusion.
The proposed stabilization mechanism applies when constituent elements have relatively similar atomic sizes and bonding characteristics.
Reactive environments or large atomic-size disparities may introduce additional stabilization or degradation mechanisms.
Prior evidence supports a stabilizing effect of high configurational entropy.
Atomic strain and surface segregation may overlap with configurational-entropy effects in some regimes.
